31	/**
32	 * Lakeview Labs & Kidney Care: FOLIO export, version 1.
33	 *
34	 * Lakeview runs an outreach reference laboratory and a nephrology clinic on one system. The export is a
35	 * row-for-row copy of that system's tables. Every payload entry is one table row; its `type` is the table
36	 * name. Column names are the database's own (UPPER_SNAKE). Codes are Lakeview's, documented below; the
37	 * tables at the end of this file list every code value in use.
38	 *
39	 * Two kinds of item, each with its own entry type:
40	 *
41	 * - **Lab report items** (`LabReportRow`): one item per requisition, i.e. one set of specimens drawn at
42	 *   one time for one ordering client. Holds exactly one LAB_REQ row, one LAB_ORDER row per ordered test,
43	 *   and the LAB_RESULT rows those orders produced. Published when every order on the requisition is
44	 *   resulted, cancelled or void (rarely earlier, with 'P' rows, when a slow test holds up a requisition
45	 *   with urgent results). Lab items have no author (system-generated) and no narrative.
46	 * - **Clinic contact items** (`ClinicRow`): one item per nephrology clinic contact (office visit or
47	 *   telephone contact). Holds exactly one CLINIC_VISIT row plus the VISIT_DX, VITAL, MED_ORDER and
48	 *   MED_STATUS_HIST rows entered during that contact. The narrative is the note the nephrologist typed
49	 *   and signed; it is short and is never generated from the rows.
50	 *
51	 * Changes: rows are never edited in place in the export. When a row changes after its item was
52	 * published (a result invalidated, an order marked entered in error), Lakeview publishes a new item that
53	 * `supersedes` the old one and restates every row of the requisition or contact with current values.
54	 * Exception: a medication's status changes are separate MED_STATUS_HIST rows in a later contact, not a
55	 * re-published MED_ORDER row. See MED_ORDER.MED_STATUS.
56	 *
57	 * Times: every timestamp column is RFC 3339 with the UTC offset in effect in America/Chicago at that
58	 * moment (e.g. `2026-02-09T08:14:00-06:00`). Date-only columns are local calendar dates.
59	 *
60	 * Identifiers: REQ_ID, ORDER_ID, RESULT_ID, ACCESSION, VISIT_ID, RX_ID and HIST_ID are Lakeview-assigned,
61	 * never reused, and unique across the whole export (not only within an item). Rows refer to rows in
62	 * other items by these ids.
63	 */
64	
65	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
66	// Lab report items
67	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
68	
69	/** One row in a lab report item. */
70	export type LabReportRow = LabReq | LabOrder | LabResult;
71	
72	/** The requisition: who ordered, when the specimens were drawn. Exactly one per lab report item. */
73	export interface LabReq {
74	  type: 'LAB_REQ';
75	
76	  /** Requisition id, e.g. "RQ-2602090412". */
77	  REQ_ID: string;
78	
79	  /**
80	   * Ordering client account code. Clients are practices that send work to Lakeview.
81	   * - 'NGFM': Northgate Family Medicine (outside primary care practice).
82	   * - 'LVNEPH': Lakeview's own nephrology clinic.
83	   * Other client codes exist for other patients; CLIENT_NAME always carries the display name.
84	   */
85	  CLIENT_CODE: string;
86	
87	  /** Display name of the ordering client, as on the requisition. */
88	  CLIENT_NAME: string;
89	
90	  /** NPI of the ordering clinician, 10 digits. Absent when the requisition was standing-order only. */
91	  ORDERING_NPI?: string;
92	
93	  /** Ordering clinician's name, "Last, First Credential", as typed on the requisition. */
94	  ORDERING_NAME?: string;
95	
96	  /**
97	   * When the specimens were drawn. This is the clinically meaningful time and the item's `effective`.
98	   * All specimens on one requisition share it.
99	   */
100	  COLLECTED_AT: string;
101	
102	  /** When the specimens were logged in at the laboratory. */
103	  RECEIVED_AT: string;
104	
105	  /**
106	   * Patient-reported fasting status at draw.
107	   * - 'Y': fasting at least 8 hours.
108	   * - 'N': not fasting.
109	   * - 'U': not asked or not recorded.
110	   */
111	  FASTING: 'Y' | 'N' | 'U';
112	}
113	
114	/**
115	 * One ordered test or panel on the requisition. One row per order, even when two orders are run on the
116	 * same tube (they then share an ACCESSION).
117	 */
118	export interface LabOrder {
119	  type: 'LAB_ORDER';
120	
121	  /** Order id, e.g. "OR-7730412". */
122	  ORDER_ID: string;
123	
124	  /** The LAB_REQ this order belongs to (always the LAB_REQ in the same item). */
125	  REQ_ID: string;
126	
127	  /**
128	   * What was ordered: a Lakeview test code (see `LabTestCode` at the end of this file). An order code
129	   * may produce several result rows: panel codes (e.g. 'LK-CBC') produce one row per component, and
130	   * 'LK-CREAT' also produces calculated eGFR rows.
131	   */
132	  ORDER_CODE: `${LabTestCode}`;
133	
134	  /** Display name of the ordered test as printed on the requisition. */
135	  ORDER_NAME: string;
136	
137	  /**
138	   * Specimen container barcode, "LV" + 2-digit year, day of year, 5-digit sequence, e.g. "LV26-040-00093".
139	   * One accession per tube; several orders can share one. Outside systems that receive Lakeview results
140	   * (e.g. Northgate) keep this number as their link back to Lakeview.
141	   */
142	  ACCESSION: string;
143	
144	  /**
145	   * Specimen type.
146	   * - 'SER': serum.
147	   * - 'PLA': plasma (lithium heparin).
148	   * - 'WB': whole blood (EDTA).
149	   * - 'URN': random urine.
150	   */
151	  SPECIMEN_TYPE: 'SER' | 'PLA' | 'WB' | 'URN';
152	
153	  /**
154	   * Specimen condition noted on receipt or by the analyzer.
155	   * - 'OK': acceptable.
156	   * - 'HEM': hemolyzed. Potassium, AST and LDH can be falsely high. Results are still released, with a
157	   *   comment; a recollection is usually requested.
158	   * - 'LIP': lipemic.
159	   * - 'ICT': icteric.
160	   * - 'QNS': quantity not sufficient; affected results have RESULT_STATUS 'X'.
161	   * - 'CLT': clotted.
162	   */
163	  SPECIMEN_COND: 'OK' | 'HEM' | 'LIP' | 'ICT' | 'QNS' | 'CLT';
164	
165	  /**
166	   * Where the order stands in the lab workflow. Integer code. This is a separate axis from each result
167	   * row's RESULT_STATUS: an order is 4 (resulted) as soon as its results have been released, and stays 4
168	   * even if one of its results is later invalidated (RESULT_STATUS 'C'). Never infer result validity from
169	   * this field.
170	   * - 1: ordered, not yet collected.
171	   * - 2: collected, in transit or awaiting testing.
172	   * - 3: in process (some results may be preliminary).
173	   * - 4: resulted (results released).
174	   * - 5: cancelled before testing (no results; see STATUS_REASON).
175	   * - 9: entered in error (wrong patient, duplicate order). The order is void. Any result rows it has
176	   *      were produced by the analyzer before the error was caught, still carry their own
177	   *      RESULT_STATUS (often 'F'), and must not be used.
178	   */
179	  ORDER_STATUS: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 9;
180	
181	  /** When ORDER_STATUS last changed. */
182	  STATUS_AT: string;
183	
184	  /** Free-text reason entered with status 5 or 9, e.g. "Duplicate order". Absent for other statuses. */
185	  STATUS_REASON?: string;
186	
187	  /**
188	   * Set when this order is a repeat draw of an earlier order (in an earlier requisition): that order's
189	   * ORDER_ID. Absent for ordinary orders.
190	   */
191	  REPEAT_OF_ORDER_ID?: string;
192	
193	  /**
194	   * Why the repeat draw was taken. Present exactly when REPEAT_OF_ORDER_ID is.
195	   * - 'HEM': the earlier specimen was hemolyzed. The earlier result is normally invalidated
196	   *   (RESULT_STATUS 'C', REPLACED_BY_RESULT_ID pointing here).
197	   * - 'CONF': confirmation of a critical or unexpected value. Both results stand; the earlier one is
198	   *   NOT invalidated.
199	   * - 'QNS': the earlier specimen was insufficient.
200	   */
201	  REPEAT_REASON?: 'HEM' | 'CONF' | 'QNS';
202	}
203	
204	/**
205	 * One reported result value. Lakeview stores every result as text (VALUE_TEXT) plus a numeric
206	 * convenience column (VALUE_NUM). VALUE_TEXT is the value of record.
207	 */
208	export interface LabResult {
209	  type: 'LAB_RESULT';
210	
211	  /** Result id, e.g. "RS-90044817". */
212	  RESULT_ID: string;
213	
214	  /** The LAB_ORDER that produced this row (always in the same item). */
215	  ORDER_ID: string;
216	
217	  /**
218	   * Lakeview test code for this result (see `LabTestCode`). Codes are stable across years but are
219	   * retired and replaced when the method or equation changes: eGFR changed code on 2022-01-10. A
220	   * mapper that needs a continuous series must join the old and new codes.
221	   */
222	  TEST_CODE: `${LabTestCode}`;
223	
224	  /** Test name as printed on the report on the day it was resulted. Wording varies over the years. */
225	  TEST_NAME: string;
226	
227	  /**
228	   * LOINC code, copied from Lakeview's code table at the moment the row was resulted. Absent when the
229	   * test code had no LOINC mapping at that moment, which includes some codes that are mapped now (rows
230	   * resulted before the mapping was added are not back-filled). `LabTestCode` says which codes
231	   * have a mapping and since when. Do not use LOINC as the only key to find a test; use TEST_CODE.
232	   */
233	  LOINC?: string;
234	
235	  /**
236	   * The result as reported, as text. Usually a plain decimal ("1.45", "212"). May carry a comparator
237	   * (">60", "<0.1", ">90") or be non-numeric ("Not done: QNS", "See comment"). Never sort or compare as
238	   * text.
239	   */
240	  VALUE_TEXT: string;
241	
242	  /**
243	   * Numeric form of VALUE_TEXT, for queries.
244	   * - A number when VALUE_TEXT is a plain decimal: the same value.
245	   * - 9999999 (sentinel) when VALUE_TEXT has a comparator such as ">60": the number is NOT the value;
246	   *   read VALUE_TEXT.
247	   * - null when VALUE_TEXT is not numeric.
248	   */
249	  VALUE_NUM: number | null;
250	
251	  /**
252	   * Unit of VALUE_TEXT, as Lakeview prints it (see `LakeviewUnit`). Fixed per TEST_CODE. Null only when
253	   * VALUE_TEXT is not numeric. Note 'K/uL' means thousands per microlitre: a platelet count of "212" is
254	   * 212 000 cells/uL.
255	   */
256	  UNIT_CODE: `${LakeviewUnit}` | null;
257	
258	  /** Reference interval as printed, e.g. "3.5-5.1", "<30", ">59". Text; may be absent for calculated tests. */
259	  REF_RANGE_TEXT?: string;
260	
261	  /**
262	   * Abnormal flag against the reference interval.
263	   * - 'N': within range.
264	   * - 'L' / 'H': below / above range.
265	   * - 'LL' / 'HH': critical low / high (phoned to the ordering clinician).
266	   * - 'A': abnormal, non-numeric.
267	   * Absent when the test has no reference interval or the value is not numeric.
268	   */
269	  ABN_FLAG?: 'N' | 'L' | 'H' | 'LL' | 'HH' | 'A';
270	
271	  /**
272	   * Validity of this row's value. Letter code. Independent of the order's ORDER_STATUS.
273	   * - 'P': preliminary; a later item will restate the row as 'F'.
274	   * - 'F': final.
275	   * - 'A': amended; the value on this row was changed after it was final (for example a transcription
276	   *   fix). The value shown is the current, valid one; the earlier value is in the superseded item.
277	   * - 'C': corrected away. The value on this row has been withdrawn and must not be used. If a
278	   *   replacement exists, REPLACED_BY_RESULT_ID names it (usually in a repeat-draw requisition). Note:
279	   *   this is NOT the HL7 v2 meaning of 'C' (where 'C' marks the new corrected value); in Lakeview 'C'
280	   *   marks the old, withdrawn one.
281	   * - 'X': not performed (cancelled, QNS); VALUE_TEXT says why, VALUE_NUM is null.
282	   */
283	  RESULT_STATUS: 'P' | 'F' | 'A' | 'C' | 'X';
284	
285	  /** When the value was released (first released, for 'A' and 'C' rows). */
286	  RESULTED_AT: string;
287	
288	  /** When RESULT_STATUS was set to 'A' or 'C'. Absent otherwise. */
289	  STATUS_CHANGED_AT?: string;
290	
291	  /** For RESULT_STATUS 'C': the RESULT_ID of the row that replaces this one. Absent if no replacement. */
292	  REPLACED_BY_RESULT_ID?: string;
293	
294	  /**
295	   * For calculated results: the RESULT_ID of the row it was calculated from (same item): the
296	   * creatinine row for eGFR, the total cholesterol row for calculated LDL (LK-LDLC).
297	   * Lakeview calculates eGFR from creatinine, the patient's age and sex on the collection date, and,
298	   * for the 2009 codes only, a race coefficient (both race variants are always reported; the lab
299	   * does not know the patient's race).
300	   */
301	  DERIVED_FROM_RESULT_ID?: string;
302	
303	  /** Result comment as printed on the report, free text. Lakeview's comments are canned phrases. */
304	  COMMENT_TEXT?: string;
305	}

307	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
308	// Clinic contact items
309	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
310	
311	/** One row in a nephrology clinic contact item. */
312	export type ClinicRow = ClinicVisit | VisitDx | Vital | MedOrder | MedStatusHist;
313	
314	/** The clinic contact itself. Exactly one per clinic contact item. */
315	export interface ClinicVisit {
316	  type: 'CLINIC_VISIT';
317	
318	  /** Contact id, e.g. "NV-104552". */
319	  VISIT_ID: string;
320	
321	  /**
322	   * Kind of contact.
323	   * - 'NP': new patient office visit.
324	   * - 'FU': follow-up office visit.
325	   * - 'TEL': telephone contact (no vitals; CKD_G / CKD_A usually absent).
326	   */
327	  VISIT_TYPE: 'NP' | 'FU' | 'TEL';
328	
329	  /** Start of the contact. The item's `effective`. */
330	  VISIT_AT: string;
331	
332	  /** NPI of the nephrologist responsible for the contact. */
333	  PROVIDER_NPI: string;
334	
335	  /**

355

613	 * Consumer views, version 2: the small shapes a patient-facing chart app reads.

615	 * These are defined by the consumer, not by any source. A mapper turns one source's FOLIO record items

617	 * reports only what its own source says, and never invents, infers from other sources, or "corrects"

622	 * `asOf` date. It returns the rows that describe that source's record as it stood at the end of that
623	 * date.

628	 *   the `asOf` day in America/Chicago. Ignore items recorded later. Apply the FOLIO correction rules to
629	 *   the items in scope: an item listed in another in-scope item's `supersedes` or `retracts` (same

`out/transform.ts` type-checks and runs on the sample patient. The output looks right: finerenone held since 2021-10-08, CKD G3a/A3 with diabetes and hypertension as active problems, and the invalidated hemolyzed potassium left out. I only ran it as of 2024-01-01, and I didn't write tests for the situations the samples don't show, such as drug-caused diagnoses.

Judgment calls:
- **Scope and corrections:** I keep an item only if its `recorded` date, converted to America/Chicago, is on or before `asOf`. Anything named in another in-scope item's `supersedes` or `retracts` is dropped.
- **Labs:**
  - **Order and result status:** I use only orders with status 3 or 4. I use results with status P (preliminary) or F/A (final). Results marked C or X, and orders cancelled or entered in error, are skipped.
  - **eGFR:** I report only the non-race variants (`LK-EGFR09N` and `LK-EGFR21`). I take the equation from the result's comment text first, then from the code. I leave the LOINC off the 2009 eGFR rows, because Lakeview's mapping there is an MDRD code, which is wrong for that equation.
  - **Values:** I parse the comparator from `VALUE_TEXT` and ignore the 9999999 sentinel. Platelet and WBC units become `10*3/uL`. Rows are deduplicated by `RESULT_ID`, keeping the most advanced status. Chloride, BUN and the other analytes Lakeview doesn't offer are not reported.
- **Vitals:** Each clinic visit gives one row timed at its first systolic BP. A second BP reading goes in the `repeat_*` fields. Weight is rounded to one decimal.
- **Problems:**
  - **Grouping and status:** The latest diagnosis per ICD code wins, and all N18.x codes are treated as one CKD condition. Only active (A) and history (H) diagnoses are reported. Provisional and ruled-out ones are not.
  - **CKD stage:** `ckd_stage` and `albuminuria` come from that visit's `CKD_G` and `CKD_A`, falling back to the ICD code and then the latest visit that has them.
  - **Onset:** The structured data has no onset, so I read "since …" from the narrative span attached to the diagnosis entry.
- **Drug-caused diagnoses:** T-codes ("adverse effect of X") produce an allergy row only. "X-associated" diagnoses produce both a problem and an allergy row. If the diagnosis names only a drug class and exactly one drug of that class is in the same item, I use that drug. Reaction type and mechanism are keyword-based, and I default to `unknown` when unsure.
- **Medications:** Current status is the latest `MED_STATUS_HIST` row, otherwise the `MED_ORDER` status. A prescription that was ever entered in error (status 9) is dropped, and IV orders are excluded. There is one row per ingredient, taken from the line with the latest event. The stop reason is mapped from `REASON_CODE`.
